synthesis the carded evidence: one randomised placebo-controlled trial (n = 78) and its open-label extension (45 continuers, up to 5.5 years), one systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials in patients not candidates for surgery (11 medical-therapy trials, 438 patients), and one systematic review of medical management (54 included studies). unique randomised participants in the cinacalcet programme total 78, so no small-n stamp labelling applies. against placebo, cinacalcet normalised calcium (73% vs 5%) but bone mineral density was unchanged, while bone turnover markers rose (peacock 2005). over up to 5.5 years of treatment, density z-scores at spine, hip and wrist did not change (peacock 2009). in the population this shelf asks about — patients not candidates for or declining surgery — a randomised-trial meta-analysis attributes bone-density increases to alendronate, denosumab, vitamin d and estrogen, not to cinacalcet (ye 2022), and a medical-management review states plainly that bisphosphonates improved density while cinacalcet had no effect (leere 2017). no carded record reports fractures on cinacalcet. proposed possible (the treatment made no difference to bone density) — a calcium drug, not a bone drug, on the carded evidence. absence of a density effect is not proof of absence of any bone effect — density was a secondary outcome, follow-up in the controlled trial was about a year, and fractures were never reported; but after 5.5 years and two reviews, a clinically useful bone benefit should have shown itself if it were large. synthesis of peacock m et al. the journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 2005 (pmid: 15522938); peacock m et al. the journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 2009 (pmid: 19837909); ye z et al. journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the american society for bone and mineral research. 2022 (pmid: 36053960); leere js et al. frontiers in endocrinology. 2017 (pmid: 28473803).

shelves.title: Levothyroxine and cardiovascular events at 80-plus (PARTIAL completion of live #354's symptom question): SPLIT — the pooled randomised trials (including IEMO 80-plus) show no cardiovascular reduction, while a large observational analysis claims one
shelves.question: In adults over 80 with subclinical hypothyroidism, does levothyroxine reduce cardiovascular events versus observation?
shelves.mesh: Aged · Aged, 80 and over · Cardiovascular Diseases · Double-Blind Method · Europe · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Hypothyroidism · Male · Overtreatment · Prognosis · Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic · Thyroxine
shelves.balance: SPLIT — the randomised evidence says no cardiovascular benefit; a large observational analysis says the opposite, and the designs are not equal. The pooled individual-participant analysis of the two randomised trials (TRUST, age 65 and over, n = 737; IEMO 80-plus, age 80 and over, n = 105; 842 participants in total) found levothyroxine did not significantly change cardiovascular events (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.41-1.25), atrial fibrillation (HR 0.69), heart failure (HR 0.41) or all-cause mortality (HR 1.28), irrespective of cardiovascular history and age (Zijlstra 2021). A meta-analysis of 7 studies (21,055 adults) likewise found no association with all-cause (pooled RR 0.95) or cardiovascular (pooled RR 0.99) mortality, and specifically no association in the older subgroup (Peng 2021). Against that, a UK emulated target trial of 22,621 adults over 50 (median age 66 — not an over-80 population) reported lower cardiovascular risk on levothyroxine (adjusted HR 0.82), with benefit limited to patients above age-specific TSH ranges and after at least 5 years of treatment (Holley 2026) — an observational design open to the confounding the randomised trials were built to remove. PARTIAL completion: live shelf #354 covers subclinical hypothyroidism treatment for symptoms, tiredness and quality of life (TRUST and the 80-plus symptom analysis are carded there and are NOT re-carded here); this shelf covers the cardiovascular-events outcome, including the 80-plus trial's contribution to the pooled randomised analysis. For the over-80 cardiovascular question specifically, the only randomised data are the pooled analysis above, and they show no reduction (the treatment made no difference). PROPOSED SPLIT (randomised: no benefit; observational: apparent benefit).

cards.headline: Zijlstra 2021: pooling the two randomised trials (842 participants, including the 105-person 80-plus trial), levothyroxine did not significantly change cardiovascular events (HR 0.74), atrial fibrillation, heart failure or mortality — irrespective of age
cards.summary: Zijlstra 2021: pooling the two randomised trials (842 participants, including the 105-person 80-plus trial), levothyroxine did not significantly change cardiovascular events (HR 0.74), atrial fibrillation, heart failure or mortality — irrespective of age
cards.type: Pooled individual-participant analysis of two randomised placebo-controlled trials (Zijlstra 2021)
cards.people: One-stage individual-participant pooled analysis of two parallel randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials: TRUST (737 participants aged 65 and over) and IEMO80+ (105 participants aged 80 and over), all with subclinical hypothyroidism (elevated TSH, free T4 in range). Median age 75.0 years; 448 (53.2%) women; mean baseline TSH 6.38 mIU/L; median levothyroxine dose 50 µg, titrated to TSH in range.
cards.result: At 1 year TSH was 3.66 mIU/L on levothyroxine versus 5.66 on placebo (P < 0.001). Levothyroxine did not significantly change any prespecified cardiovascular outcome: cardiovascular events HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.41-1.25), new atrial fibrillation HR 0.69 (0.32-1.52), heart failure HR 0.41 (0.13-1.35), all-cause mortality HR 1.28 (0.54-3.03) — irrespective of history of cardiovascular disease and age. Every interval crosses 1: on the randomised evidence, the treatment made no difference to cardiovascular outcomes.
cards.watchOut: The 80-plus trial contributes only 105 of the 842 participants, so the over-80 stratum on its own is small and the pooled intervals are wide — the honest reading is 'no benefit shown, including at 80-plus', not 'benefit at 80-plus excluded with precision'.

Frontiers in Endocrinology. 2021. PMID: 34093444. Registry ID: NCT01660126 (also NTR3851, as printed in the record). cards.headline: Peng 2021: across 7 studies and 21,055 adults, thyroid hormone therapy was not associated with all-cause (RR 0.95) or cardiovascular (RR 0.99) mortality — and specifically not in older adults
cards.summary: Peng 2021: across 7 studies and 21,055 adults, thyroid hormone therapy was not associated with all-cause (RR 0.95) or cardiovascular (RR 0.99) mortality — and specifically not in older adults
cards.people: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies comparing thyroid hormone therapy with placebo or no therapy in adults with subclinical hypothyroidism, searched to April 2020: 5 observational studies and 2 randomised trials, 21,055 adults.
cards.result: Overall, thyroid hormone therapy was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality (pooled relative risk 0.95, 95% CI 0.75-1.22; P = .704) or cardiovascular mortality (pooled relative risk 0.99, 95% CI 0.82-1.20; P = .946). In younger adults (under 65-70 years) therapy was associated with lower all-cause (RR 0.50) and cardiovascular (RR 0.54) mortality, but no significant association was observed in older adults (aged 65-70 and over). The authors conclude therapy does not provide protective effects on mortality in older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism.
cards.watchOut: Five of the seven pooled studies are observational, so the pooled null for older adults is mostly non-randomised evidence agreeing with the randomised pooled analysis — agreement that strengthens the direction but not beyond what the randomised card already shows.
cards.source: Peng CC et al. Association of Thyroid Hormone Therapy with Mortality in Subclinical Hypothyroidism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism. 2021. PMID: 33107557. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Holley 2026 (ACEL-UK): in an observational emulated target trial of 22,621 adults over 50, levothyroxine was associated with fewer cardiovascular events (adjusted HR 0.82) and lower mortality (HR 0.71) — the opposite direction from the randomised trials
cards.summary: Holley 2026 (ACEL-UK): in an observational emulated target trial of 22,621 adults over 50, levothyroxine was associated with fewer cardiovascular events (adjusted HR 0.82) and lower mortality (HR 0.71) — the opposite direction from the randomised trials
cards.people: Observational emulated target trial using UK primary-care records (The Health Improvement Network), 2006-2022: 22,621 adults over 50 with subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH 4.1-10.0 mU/L, free T4 in range); median age 66 years; 76.7% women; 62% prescribed levothyroxine and 38% not. Hazard ratios adjusted by inverse probability of treatment weighting. This is a general over-50 population, not an over-80 population.
cards.result: Levothyroxine was associated with reduced cardiovascular events (adjusted HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.91) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.71, 0.67-0.75), with no adverse bone effect (adjusted HR 1.04, 0.93-1.17). Cardiovascular benefits were limited to patients with TSH above the age-specific range and after at least 5 years of treatment. The authors conclude age-specific TSH levels should guide treatment decisions.
cards.watchOut: People prescribed levothyroxine in routine care differ from people not prescribed it in ways records capture imperfectly, and a mortality HR of 0.71 is larger than plausible drug effects usually survive randomisation — this card is the observational side of a genuine split, printed so readers can see it, weighted below the randomised cards.
cards.source: Holley M et al. Assessing the Cardiovascular Effects of Levothyroxine Use in an Ageing UK Population with Subclinical Hypothyroidism: Emulated Target Trial (ACEL-UK-ETT). Thyroid. 2026. cards.headline: Synthesis: for cardiovascular events at 80-plus, the randomised answer is no reduction; the observational literature disagrees, and the split is a design split
cards.summary: Synthesis: for cardiovascular events at 80-plus, the randomised answer is no reduction; the observational literature disagrees, and the split is a design split
cards.people: The carded evidence: a pooled individual-participant analysis of the two randomised trials (842 participants, 105 aged 80-plus), a mortality meta-analysis (7 studies, 21,055 adults), and one large observational emulated target trial (22,621 adults over 50). Total carded participants exceed 40,000, so no small-N stamp labelling applies — though the randomised over-80 stratum itself is only 105 people, printed on the first card.
cards.result: Randomised: cardiovascular events HR 0.74 (0.41-1.25), mortality HR 1.28 — no significant effect at any age (Zijlstra 2021); meta-analysis: no mortality association in older adults (Peng 2021). Observational: cardiovascular adjusted HR 0.82 and mortality HR 0.71 favouring treatment (Holley 2026). PROPOSED SPLIT (randomised: no benefit; observational: apparent benefit).
cards.watchOut: A 2026 systematic review on this exact question (PMID: 41922998) was identified at build and deliberately NOT carded: its PubMed record lists it as a Retracted Publication. The split on this shelf rests only on the three records above.

shelves.title: rhTSH versus thyroid hormone withdrawal for radioiodine ablation (PARTIAL completion of pack #2901): ablation success equivalent, quality of life better with rhTSH
shelves.question: In adults with low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer after thyroidectomy, does preparation with recombinant human TSH work as well as thyroid hormone withdrawal for radioactive iodine ablation success?
shelves.mesh: Ablation Techniques · Adenocarcinoma, Follicular · Adult · Carcinoma, Papillary · Combined Modality Therapy · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Humans · Hypothyroidism · Iodine Radioisotopes · Male · Middle Aged · Neck · Quality of Life · Thyroid Hormones · Thyroid Neoplasms · Thyroidectomy · Thyrotropin · Treatment Outcome · Ultrasonography
shelves.balance: PARTIAL completion: pack #2901 already answers the neighbouring question — low-dose versus high-dose radioiodine, both prepared with thyrotropin alfa — and its HiLo card reports that trial's factorial preparation comparison as a secondary slice; the homed HiLo record is not re-carded here and no figures are taken from it. This shelf answers the uncovered slice head-on: the preparation-method comparison itself. Two randomised trials and a meta-analysis agree that ablation success is equivalent: in ESTIMABL (752 enrolled, 684 evaluable) ablation was complete in 92% overall and the rate was equivalent between recombinant human TSH (rhTSH) and thyroid hormone withdrawal; in the earlier international trial the strict ablation criterion was met by 100% of both groups (Pacini 2006); and pooling seven trials (1,325 patients) found no significant difference in ablation success (odds ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.56 to 1.37), with better quality of life and fewer adverse events on rhTSH. PROPOSED LIKELY: rhTSH preparation works as well as withdrawal for ablation success in low-risk disease, while sparing patients the hypothyroid interval — concordant randomised evidence, with the equivalence shown in two independent large trials.

cards.headline: ESTIMABL 2012: in 752 patients with low-risk thyroid cancer, ablation success was equivalent with recombinant human TSH and with thyroid hormone withdrawal (92% complete ablation overall)
cards.summary: ESTIMABL 2012: in 752 patients with low-risk thyroid cancer, ablation success was equivalent with recombinant human TSH and with thyroid hormone withdrawal (92% complete ablation overall)
cards.people: 752 patients aged 18 or older after total thyroidectomy for low-risk differentiated thyroid carcinoma (92% papillary), randomised in a 2-by-2 design to thyrotropin stimulation by thyroid hormone withdrawal or by recombinant human TSH, and to radioiodine activities of 1.1 GBq or 3.7 GBq; ablation was assessed 8 months later by neck ultrasonography and rhTSH-stimulated thyroglobulin, with 684 patients evaluable.
cards.result: Thyroid ablation was complete in 631 of 684 patients (92%). The ablation rate was equivalent between the two radioiodine activities and between the two thyrotropin-stimulation methods, under the trial's prespecified equivalence framework: neck ultrasonography was normal in 95% of evaluable patients, and among those without thyroglobulin antibodies the stimulated thyroglobulin was 1.0 ng/mL or less in 95%. There were no unexpected serious adverse events. The authors conclude that rhTSH preparation with low-dose radioiodine may be sufficient for managing low-risk thyroid cancer.
cards.watchOut: ESTIMABL's population is strictly low-risk disease and its ablation endpoint is an 8-month surrogate (imaging plus stimulated thyroglobulin), not recurrence or survival; equivalence here does not automatically extend to higher-risk cancers or to ablation of known residual disease.
cards.source: Schlumberger M et al. Strategies of radioiodine ablation in patients with low-risk thyroid cancer. The New England journal of medicine. 2012. PMID: 22551127. Registry ID: NCT00435851. cards.headline: Pacini 2006: remnant ablation succeeded in 100% of both preparation groups, with better quality of life and a third less radiation dose to blood on recombinant human TSH
cards.summary: Pacini 2006: remnant ablation succeeded in 100% of both preparation groups, with better quality of life and a third less radiation dose to blood on recombinant human TSH
cards.people: Patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma after surgery in an international randomised multicentre trial, prepared for remnant ablation with 3.7 GBq radioiodine either with recombinant human TSH while continuing thyroid hormone (euthyroid group) or by thyroid hormone withdrawal (hypothyroid group). Total enrolment: N not documented in the record; the thyroglobulin-criterion analysis reports 24 euthyroid and 21 hypothyroid patients.
cards.result: The predefined primary ablation criterion (no visible thyroid-bed uptake, or fractional uptake below 0.1% on neck scans at 8 months) was satisfied in 100% of patients in both groups. The secondary criterion (rhTSH-stimulated thyroglobulin below 2 ng/mL) was met by 23 of 24 euthyroid patients (96%) and 18 of 21 hypothyroid patients (86%) (P=0.23). Quality of life was better preserved in the euthyroid group (significantly higher SF-36 scores in five of eight categories, and fewer hypothyroid symptoms), and radiation dose to the blood was one third lower with rhTSH preparation.
cards.watchOut: A small, early trial using the high (3.7 GBq) radioiodine activity in all patients; its 100% success in both arms leaves no room to detect a difference, so it supports — but cannot alone establish — equivalence; ESTIMABL is the decisive trial.

cards.headline: Fu 2015 meta-analysis: pooling 7 trials (1,325 patients), ablation success did not differ between rhTSH and withdrawal (odds ratio 0.87), while quality of life favoured rhTSH
cards.summary: Fu 2015 meta-analysis: pooling 7 trials (1,325 patients), ablation success did not differ between rhTSH and withdrawal (odds ratio 0.87), while quality of life favoured rhTSH
cards.people: Seven randomised controlled trials comprising 1,325 patients with differentiated thyroid cancer undergoing radioiodine remnant ablation, comparing recombinant human TSH preparation with thyroid hormone withdrawal (and, secondarily, low versus high radioiodine activities under rhTSH).
cards.result: Successful ablation rates did not differ significantly between rhTSH and withdrawal preparation (odds ratio 0.87, 95% CI 0.56 to 1.37; P=0.56). rhTSH preparation gave significantly better health-related quality of life (mean difference 3.59, 95% CI 2.81 to 4.37), fewer adverse events during and after ablation (odds ratio 0.57, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.73), and lower radiation exposure to blood and bone marrow. No deaths or serious adverse effects occurred with either preparation, with maximum follow-up of 12 months in the included trials.
cards.watchOut: The pooled trials include the two trials carded above and use ablation surrogates with at most 12 months of follow-up; none investigated recurrence, secondary malignancy or cost outcomes, so the equivalence claim is about ablation success, not long-term cancer outcomes.

cards.headline: Synthesis: recombinant human TSH preparation ablates the remnant as successfully as thyroid hormone withdrawal — and patients feel better getting there
cards.summary: Synthesis: recombinant human TSH preparation ablates the remnant as successfully as thyroid hormone withdrawal — and patients feel better getting there
cards.people: The carded evidence: two randomised trials (752 enrolled in ESTIMABL; Pacini 2006, total N not documented in the record) and one meta-analysis of seven trials (1,325 patients, overlapping the trials). The dose-comparison question is homed on pack #2901 and is not re-carded here.
cards.result: Ablation success was equivalent between preparation methods in ESTIMABL (92% complete ablation overall) and identical on the strict criterion in Pacini 2006 (100% in both groups); the pooled odds ratio was 0.87 (95% CI 0.56 to 1.37), consistent with no meaningful difference. rhTSH additionally improved quality of life, reduced adverse events (pooled odds ratio 0.57) and lowered radiation exposure to blood. PROPOSED LIKELY: rhTSH works as well as withdrawal for ablation success in low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer.
cards.watchOut: Every source measures ablation success within about a year; whether preparation method affects recurrence over decades is untested, and these trials were run in low-risk disease — the population in whom many clinicians now omit ablation altogether.

shelves.title: Thyroid hormone replacement in nonthyroidal illness: no survival benefit in the small old trials, and a 2024 septic-shock pilot split in opposite directions by subgroup - weak, mixed evidence
shelves.question: In critically ill patients with nonthyroidal illness, does thyroid hormone replacement (T4 or T3), compared with no replacement, improve survival or organ outcomes?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Aged · Critical Care · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Mortality · Peptidyl-Dipeptidase A/blood · Prospective Studies · Random Allocation · Talc · Thyrotropin/blood · Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone · Thyroxine/blood,therapeutic use · Triiodothyronine/blood
shelves.balance: MAYBE (weak evidence) - the base is small, old and scattered, and it is presented as weak/mixed, not settled. The only trial in the exact population (Brent & Hershman 1986) randomised just 23 intensive-care patients with severe nonthyroidal illness and low T4: mortality was 73% on T4 against 75% on control (the treatment made no difference), and T4 suppressed TSH and delayed the spontaneous T3 rise of recovery. Klemperer 1995 (142 high-risk bypass patients - an adjacent population whose preoperative T3 was normal) found T3 raised cardiac index (2.97 vs 2.67 L/min/m2) and lowered vascular resistance but changed neither drug requirements nor mortality/morbidity. The 2024 Kovacevic pilots in septic shock with euthyroid sick syndrome split in opposite directions: in the low-T3 subgroup, 28-day mortality was higher on T3 (75% vs 33.3%; P=0.004), while in the low-T3/low-T4 subgroup ICU mortality was lower on T3 (25% vs 52.1%; P=0.039). Two small subgroups pointing opposite ways, on top of null older trials, support no routine replacement - and counsel caution rather than enthusiasm.

cards.headline: Brent & Hershman 1986: in 23 ICU patients with severe nonthyroidal illness and low T4, mortality was 73% on T4 against 75% on control (the treatment made no difference)
cards.summary: Brent & Hershman 1986: in 23 ICU patients with severe nonthyroidal illness and low T4, mortality was 73% on T4 against 75% on control (the treatment made no difference)
cards.type: Randomised prospective trial (Brent & Hershman 1986) - N=23 (12 control, 11 T4); small-N printed on the face
cards.people: 23 patients admitted to a medical intensive care unit with severe nonthyroidal illness and a total serum T4 under 5 micrograms/dL, randomised to control (12 patients) or intravenous L-T4 1.5 micrograms/kg daily for 2 weeks (11 patients).
cards.result: Mortality was equivalent in the two groups (75% control vs 73% treatment - the treatment made no difference). In the treatment group, serum T4 and free T4 rose significantly by day 3 and were normal by day 5, but serum TSH and the TSH response to TRH fell significantly, and the spontaneous rise in serum T3 seen in controls on day 7 was delayed to day 10 in the T4 group. Survivors and non-survivors were completely separable by baseline T3-to-T4 ratio (17.0 +/- 1.8 vs 7.0 +/- 0.7 ng/microgram; P<0.001), regardless of treatment. The authors conclude T4 therapy was not beneficial and may suppress an important recovery mechanism by inhibiting TSH secretion.
cards.watchOut: N=23 - one of the smallest randomised trials in this library, from 1986, in a population with roughly three-in-four mortality. It can rule out a large benefit only loosely; its real weight is that the direction was null and the physiology (TSH suppression, delayed T3 recovery) pointed the wrong way.
cards.source: Brent GA et al. Thyroxine therapy in patients with severe nonthyroidal illnesses and low serum thyroxine concentration. The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 1986. PMID: 3011834. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Klemperer 1995: T3 after bypass surgery raised cardiac index (2.97 vs 2.67 L/min/m2; P=0.007) and lowered vascular resistance, but did not change drug needs, arrhythmia, or mortality and morbidity (the treatment made no difference to outcomes)
cards.summary: Klemperer 1995: T3 after bypass surgery raised cardiac index (2.97 vs 2.67 L/min/m2; P=0.007) and lowered vascular resistance, but did not change drug needs, arrhythmia, or mortality and morbidity (the treatment made no difference to outcomes)
cards.type: Randomised, placebo-controlled trial (Klemperer 1995, NEJM) - 142 patients after coronary-artery bypass surgery
cards.people: 142 patients with coronary artery disease and depressed left ventricular function undergoing coronary-artery bypass surgery, given intravenous triiodothyronine (0.8 microgram/kg bolus at cross-clamp removal, then 0.113 microgram/kg/hour for 6 hours) or placebo. Preoperative serum T3 was normal (mean 81 +/- 22 ng/dL) and fell 40% on bypass - an adjacent population to classic nonthyroidal illness, flagged as such.
cards.result: Mean postoperative cardiac index was higher on T3 (2.97 +/- 0.72 vs 2.67 +/- 0.61 L/min/m2; P=0.007) and systemic vascular resistance lower (1073 +/- 314 vs 1235 +/- 387 dyn.sec.cm-5; P=0.003). The groups did not differ significantly in arrhythmia incidence, need for inotropic or vasodilator therapy in the 24 hours after surgery, or perioperative mortality and morbidity. T3 concentrations became supranormal on treatment and were again similar between groups by 24 hours.
cards.watchOut: A haemodynamic-surrogate trial in surgical patients whose thyroid levels were normal before surgery: it shows T3 can move cardiac numbers without moving outcomes, and it does not directly test replacement in medical ICU patients with established nonthyroidal illness.
cards.source: Klemperer JD et al. Thyroid hormone treatment after coronary-artery bypass surgery. The New England journal of medicine. 1995. PMID: 7477166. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Kovacevic 2024 pilots: T3 in septic shock split in opposite directions - 28-day mortality 75% on T3 vs 33.3% on placebo in the low-T3 group (P=0.004), but ICU mortality 25% vs 52.1% in the low-T3/low-T4 group (P=0.039)
cards.summary: Kovacevic 2024 pilots: T3 in septic shock split in opposite directions - 28-day mortality 75% on T3 vs 33.3% on placebo in the low-T3 group (P=0.004), but ICU mortality 25% vs 52.1% in the low-T3/low-T4 group (P=0.039)
cards.type: Two pilot placebo-controlled randomised trials (Kovacevic 2024) - 95 patients with septic shock and euthyroid sick syndrome
cards.people: 95 patients with septic shock and euthyroid sick syndrome, divided by thyroid profile into a low-T3 group (48 patients; 24 randomised to oral T3 for 4 days, 24 to placebo) and a low-T3/low-T4 group (47 patients; 24 to T3, 23 to placebo). The primary outcome was 28-day survival.
cards.result: In the low-T3 population, 18 of 24 patients (75%) receiving T3 died by day 28 against 8 of 24 (33.3%) on placebo (P=0.004) - a harm signal. In the low-T3/low-T4 population, 6 of 24 patients (25%) receiving T3 died in the ICU against 12 of 23 (52.1%) on placebo (P=0.039) - a benefit signal in the opposite direction. T3 raised mean arterial pressure at days 1, 3 and 7 in the low-T3/low-T4 group only. The authors conclude the results suggest caution before initiating thyroid supplementation in septic patients.
cards.watchOut: Two pilot subgroups of about 24 patients per arm producing statistically significant results in opposite directions is the signature of small-sample noise, not of a real subgroup effect; neither subgroup result should be quoted without the other, and the trial was powered for neither.
cards.source: Kovacevic M et al. Triiodothyronine hormone supplementation therapy in septic shock patients with euthyroid sick syndrome: two pilot, placebo-controlled, randomized trials. Anaesthesia, critical care & pain medicine. 2024. PMID: 38061681. Registry ID: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05270798, from the record's databank fields. cards.headline: Synthesis: MAYBE (weak evidence) - no trial shows a survival or organ-outcome benefit from thyroid hormone replacement in nonthyroidal illness, and the newest pilot data contain a harm signal as well as a benefit signal
cards.summary: Synthesis: MAYBE (weak evidence) - no trial shows a survival or organ-outcome benefit from thyroid hormone replacement in nonthyroidal illness, and the newest pilot data contain a harm signal as well as a benefit signal
cards.people: The carded evidence is three randomised reports across four decades: Brent & Hershman 1986 (23 ICU patients, T4), Klemperer 1995 (142 bypass-surgery patients, T3), and Kovacevic 2024 (95 septic-shock patients in two pilot trials, T3). Total carded enrolment is 260 patients, in three different populations with three different regimens.
cards.result: Survival: no difference with T4 in the direct ICU trial (73% vs 75%); no difference in mortality or morbidity with T3 after bypass surgery despite better haemodynamics; and directly conflicting subgroup mortality results in septic shock (75% vs 33.3% against T3 in low-T3 patients; 25% vs 52.1% for T3 in low-T3/low-T4 patients). Organ outcomes: cardiac index improved with T3 in the surgical trial without any change in treatment needs. The consistent thread is surrogate movement without outcome benefit, plus one pilot harm signal.
cards.watchOut: Weak/mixed by construction: different hormones (T4 vs T3), routes, populations and eras. The correct clinical reading is 'unproven, with reasons for caution' - not 'proven useless', and certainly not a licence to treat the sick-euthyroid laboratory pattern.

shelves.title: Deiodinases (physiology): T4 is a prohormone — D1 and D2 strip one iodine to make active T3, D3 inactivates both hormones — so serum tests report the pool while tissues set their own T3; the common DIO2 Thr92Ala variant measurably lowers D2 conversion in humans, but what that means for combination therapy is still unsettled
shelves.question: How do the deiodinases (D1, D2, D3) control local and circulating T3 by converting T4, and what does that imply for interpreting thyroid tests and combination therapy in humans?
shelves.mesh: Adult · DNA/genetics · Female · Genetic Variation · Genotype · Health Status · *Hormone Replacement Therapy · Humans · Hypothyroidism/drug therapy,genetics,psychology · Iodide Peroxidase/genetics · Male · Polymorphism, Genetic/genetics · Polymorphism, Single Nucleotide/genetics · Predictive Value of Tests · Psychometrics · Surveys and Questionnaires · Thyroid Function Tests · Thyrotropin/blood · Thyroxine/blood,therapeutic use · Triiodothyronine/blood,therapeutic use · Iodothyronine Deiodinase Type II
shelves.balance: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING (textbook framing: Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, thyroid chapter; deiodinase physiology as synthesised by Bianco and colleagues). The textbook account: the thyroid secretes mostly T4, a prohormone. Type 1 deiodinase (D1, liver, kidney, thyroid) contributes much of the circulating T3 and clears reverse T3; type 2 deiodinase (D2, pituitary, brain, brown fat, skeletal muscle) generates T3 locally, inside the cell that will use it — so pituitary TSH feedback and brain T3 depend on D2 conversion, not just on serum levels; type 3 deiodinase (D3) inactivates T4 and T3. It follows that a normal TSH and free T4 do not guarantee identical tissue T3 in every person. The carded human genetic studies test that implication. Common D1 variation shifts serum hormone ratios measurably but explains under 2% of their variation (van der Deure 2009, 1,192 twins). The D2 Thr92Ala variant reduces D2-mediated T4-to-T3 conversion, and athyreotic patients carrying it ran lower free T3 after thyroidectomy at the same TSH on levothyroxine (Castagna 2017). In the WATTS cohort, the same variant's CC genotype was associated with worse baseline well-being on T4 alone and greater improvement when T3 was added — without any difference in circulating hormone levels (Panicker 2009). That last finding is unreplicated and contested, which is why the stamp is EMERGING: the enzymology is settled, the clinical meaning for combination therapy is not. The combination-therapy treatment question itself is homed on drug shelf #513; this shelf is the physiology underneath it. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING.

cards.headline: van der Deure 2009: in 1,192 healthy twins, the D1-785T allele meant 3.8% higher free T4 and 14.3% higher reverse T3 — real, but explaining under 2% of serum variation
cards.summary: van der Deure 2009: in 1,192 healthy twins, the D1-785T allele meant 3.8% higher free T4 and 14.3% higher reverse T3 — real, but explaining under 2% of serum variation
cards.type: Primary human genetic study (twin cohort, DIO1 variation and serum thyroid hormones)
cards.people: 1,192 healthy Danish twins with serum thyroid hormone measurements and genotyping of two type 1 deiodinase (DIO1) polymorphisms (C785T and A1814G), analysed with structural equation modelling for heritability; functional analyses of mRNA stability and D1 activity were performed in D1-transfected cells as supporting work.
cards.result: Carriers of the D1-785T allele had 3.8% higher free T4 and 14.3% higher reverse T3 levels (relative differences), resulting in a lower T3/T4 and T3/rT3 ratio and a higher rT3/T4 ratio — the signature of altered D1 handling, since D1 both produces T3 and clears reverse T3. The polymorphism explained only 0.87% of the variation in serum free T4 and 1.79% of the variation in reverse T3. The D1-A1814G polymorphism was not associated with serum levels, and no differences in D1 mRNA decay or D1 activity were observed between variants in the cell system. Common D1 variation nudges the circulating pool measurably but modestly.
cards.watchOut: Healthy twins and serum endpoints: D1's contribution to the circulating pool is what this design can see. It cannot see D2's tissue-local T3 generation, which by design leaves little trace in serum — the next two cards address that limb.
cards.source: van der Deure WM et al. The effect of genetic variation in the type 1 deiodinase gene on the interindividual variation in serum thyroid hormone levels: an investigation in healthy Danish twins. Clinical endocrinology. 2009. primary human genetic study (twin cohort, dio1 variation and serum thyroid hormones) 1,192 healthy danish twins with serum thyroid hormone measurements and genotyping of two type 1 deiodinase (dio1) polymorphisms (c785t and a1814g), analysed with structural equation modelling for heritability; functional analyses of mrna stability and d1 activity were performed in d1-transfected cells as supporting work. carriers of the d1-785t allele had 3.8% higher free t4 and 14.3% higher reverse t3 levels (relative differences), resulting in a lower t3/t4 and t3/rt3 ratio and a higher rt3/t4 ratio — the signature of altered d1 handling, since d1 both produces t3 and clears reverse t3. the polymorphism explained only 0.87% of the variation in serum free t4 and 1.79% of the variation in reverse t3. the d1-a1814g polymorphism was not associated with serum levels, and no differences in d1 mrna decay or d1 activity were observed between variants in the cell system. common d1 variation nudges the circulating pool measurably but modestly. healthy twins and serum endpoints: d1's contribution to the circulating pool is what this design can see. it cannot see d2's tissue-local t3 generation, which by design leaves little trace in serum — the next two cards address that limb. van der deure wm et al. the effect of genetic variation in the type 1 deiodinase gene on the interindividual variation in serum thyroid hormone levels: an investigation in healthy danish twins. clinical endocrinology. 2009. pmid: 18793344. registry id: none in the record. mesh: adult · cell line · denmark · female · *genetic variation · genotype · humans · iodide peroxidase/genetics · male · middle aged · polymorphism, genetic · thyroid hormones/blood · twins/blood,genetics

cards.headline: Castagna 2017: thyroidectomised patients carrying DIO2 Thr92Ala had lower free T3 after surgery at the same TSH on levothyroxine — and the variant enzyme converted less T4 to T3
cards.summary: Castagna 2017: thyroidectomised patients carrying DIO2 Thr92Ala had lower free T3 after surgery at the same TSH on levothyroxine — and the variant enzyme converted less T4 to T3
cards.type: Primary human genetic-physiology study (athyreotic cohort, DIO2 Thr92Ala and T3)
cards.people: 140 thyroidectomised subjects on levothyroxine, whose pre-surgical hormonal status was compared with their post-surgical status at similar TSH, with DIO2 genotyping in a subgroup of 102 of 140 patients (72.8%); free T3, free T4 and TSH were measured directly, and the enzymatic properties of the Thr92Ala variant were characterised in living cells and mouse models as supporting work.
cards.result: Mean post-surgery free T3 levels were significantly lower in patients carrying the mutated Thr92Ala allele(s) than in wild-type patients, in whom post-surgical free T3 was similar to pre-surgical levels; the −258 G/A DIO2 variation was not associated with hormonal alteration. Wild-type and Thr92Ala D2 shared the same subcellular localisation but differed in protein stability, and Thr92Ala reduced D2-mediated thyroxine-to-T3 conversion. The authors conclude thyroidectomised Thr92Ala carriers are at increased risk of reduced intracellular and serum T3 concentrations not adequately compensated by levothyroxine. In athyreotic humans — where every molecule of T3 must come from deiodination — a common D2 variant measurably moves T3.
cards.watchOut: The athyreotic setting is the extreme case — no thyroidal T3 secretion at all — so the effect size here bounds, rather than typifies, what the variant does in people with a working thyroid. The cell and mouse experiments in the record are supporting mechanistic work, not the card's human evidence.
cards.source: Castagna MG et al. DIO2 Thr92Ala Reduces Deiodinase-2 Activity and Serum-T3 Levels in Thyroid-Deficient Patients. The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 2017. PMID: 28324063. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Panicker 2009: the DIO2 rs225014 CC genotype (16% of 552 patients on T4) meant worse baseline well-being and greater improvement on T4/T3 — with no difference in circulating hormone levels
cards.summary: Panicker 2009: the DIO2 rs225014 CC genotype (16% of 552 patients on T4) meant worse baseline well-being and greater improvement on T4/T3 — with no difference in circulating hormone levels
cards.type: Primary human genetic study (pharmacogenetic analysis within the WATTS combination-therapy cohort)
cards.people: 552 subjects on thyroxine from the Weston Area T4 T3 Study (WATTS), genotyped for common variants in the three deiodinase genes and analysed against baseline psychological morbidity and response to combined T4/T3 therapy; the primary outcome was improvement in psychological well-being on the General Health Questionnaire 12 (GHQ-12).
cards.result: The rarer CC genotype of the rs225014 polymorphism in DIO2 was present in 16% of the study population and was associated with worse baseline GHQ scores on T4 (CC vs TT genotype: 14.1 vs 12.8, P = 0.03). The same genotype showed greater improvement on T4/T3 therapy than on T4 alone — by 2.3 GHQ points at 3 months and 1.4 points at 12 months (P = 0.03 for repeated-measures ANOVA). The polymorphism had no impact on circulating thyroid hormone levels. The authors state the results require replication — a genotype that predicts symptoms and combination-therapy response while leaving serum tests unchanged is exactly what D2's tissue-local physiology would predict, and exactly why it needs independent confirmation.
cards.watchOut: A single-cohort pharmacogenetic association with a subjective outcome, explicitly flagged by its authors as requiring replication, and other Thr92Ala association studies have been inconsistent. It is carded as the human hypothesis-generating evidence for D2's clinical relevance — not as a basis for genotype-guided prescribing.
cards.source: Panicker V et al. Common variation in the DIO2 gene predicts baseline psychological well-being and response to combination thyroxine plus triiodothyronine therapy in hypothyroid patients. The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 2009. PMID: 19190113. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: serum tests measure the pool; deiodinases decide what each tissue actually sees
cards.summary: Synthesis: serum tests measure the pool; deiodinases decide what each tissue actually sees
cards.people: Synthesis of the carded human studies, framed by Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology (thyroid chapter) and Bianco's deiodinase physiology. No new data.
cards.result: D1 helps fill and D3 helps drain the circulating T3 pool, while D2 generates T3 locally in pituitary, brain and other tissues — so TSH and free T4, the standard tests, report the pool and the pituitary's view of it, not every tissue's T3. Human genetics confirms the machinery matters at human scale: D1 variants shift serum ratios modestly (PMID 18793344); the common DIO2 Thr92Ala variant reduces conversion and lowers free T3 in athyreotic patients at unchanged TSH (PMID 28324063); and one cohort links the same variant to well-being and combination-therapy response without serum changes (PMID 19190113). Whether that should change prescribing is unresolved — the treatment question is homed on shelf #513. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING.
cards.watchOut: EMERGING is deliberate: the enzymology and the athyreotic free-T3 effect are solid human data, but the well-being/combination-therapy signal rests on one cohort and has not been consistently replicated — do not read this shelf as endorsing routine DIO2 genotyping or combination therapy.
cards.source: Synthesis of the cards on this shelf (PMIDs 18793344, 28324063, 19190113), framed by Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology. No additional source.

shelves.title: Calcium-sensing receptor (physiology): the parathyroid does not measure a fixed calcium target, it obeys a receptor — inactivating CaSR mutations reset the set-point upward (familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia), activating mutations reset it downward (autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia), proving the receptor is the thermostat
shelves.question: How does the calcium-sensing receptor set the PTH–calcium set-point, and how do human activating/inactivating CaSR disorders demonstrate the physiology?
shelves.mesh: Amino Acid Sequence · Base Sequence · Calcium/physiology · Cloning, Molecular · DNA Primers/chemistry · Gene Expression · Genes · Humans · Hypercalcemia/genetics · Hyperparathyroidism/congenital,genetics · Membrane Glycoproteins/genetics · Molecular Sequence Data · Mutation · Pedigree · RNA, Messenger/genetics · Receptors, Calcium-Sensing · Receptors, Cell Surface/genetics · Sequence Alignment · Sequence Homology, Amino Acid
shelves.balance: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED (textbook framing: Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, calcium-regulation chapter). The historical anchor is Brown and colleagues' 1993 cloning of the extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) from parathyroid tissue (Nature 1993; the cloned receptor was bovine, so it is cited here as framing, not carded — no animal evidence is carded on this shelf). In the textbook account, the CaSR on parathyroid chief cells senses ionised calcium directly: rising calcium activates the receptor and suppresses PTH secretion along a sigmoidal curve whose midpoint — the set-point — is a property of the receptor's sensitivity. The same receptor in the kidney adjusts urinary calcium excretion. Human genetics then performed the decisive experiment in both directions, and it is the carded evidence. Inactivating mutations cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia (FHH) and, in homozygotes, neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism: the gland behaves as if calcium were lower than it is, so PTH is not suppressed until calcium is abnormally high — the set-point reset upward (Pollak 1993; Chou 1995). An activating mutation does the exact opposite: the receptor over-signals at low calcium, PTH is suppressed inappropriately, and patients are hypocalcaemic (Pollak 1994). A thermostat proven by breaking it both ways. The calcilytic encaleret, which pharmacologically re-resets the receptor in autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia, is homed on drug shelf #5537; this shelf is the physiology it exploits. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.

cards.headline: Pollak 1993: inactivating mutations in the human CaSR gene cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia and neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism — the receptor 'sets' the extracellular calcium level
cards.summary: Pollak 1993: inactivating mutations in the human CaSR gene cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia and neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism — the receptor 'sets' the extracellular calcium level
cards.type: Primary human genetic study (CaSR loss-of-function in FHH/NSHPT, Pollak/Brown programme)
cards.people: Families with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia (FHH) and neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism (NSHPT) — two inherited conditions of altered calcium homeostasis — in whom the human Ca(2+)-sensing receptor gene was sequenced; one mutated receptor was expressed in Xenopus laevis oocytes as a functional assay (an expression system supporting a human genetics finding, flagged as such). The record does not print the number of families or patients (N not documented in the record).
cards.result: Three non-conservative missense mutations were reported: two in the extracellular N-terminal domain of the receptor and one in the final intracellular loop. The expressed wild-type receptor elicited large inward currents in response to perfused polyvalent cations, while the mutated protein's response was markedly attenuated — a loss of function. The authors conclude that the mammalian Ca(2+)-sensing receptor 'sets' the extracellular Ca²⁺ level and is defective in FHH and NSHPT. With a desensitised receptor, the parathyroid reads a normal calcium as low: PTH escapes suppression, serum calcium rises to a new, higher equilibrium, and renal calcium reabsorption stays inappropriately high (hypocalciuria) — the set-point, moved by a single receptor's sensitivity.
cards.watchOut: The oocyte currents are an in-vitro functional assay inside a human genetics paper — the card's evidence is the human genotype–phenotype link. Serum calcium and PTH values for individual families are not printed in the record and are not invented here; the card claims the direction and mechanism, which the record states explicitly.
cards.source: Pollak MR et al. Mutations in the human Ca(2+)-sensing receptor gene cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia and neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism. Cell. 1993. PMID: 7916660. Registry ID: none in the record (the record lists GenBank sequence accessions, not a trial registry). cards.headline: Pollak 1994: a single activating CaSR mutation (Glu128Ala) caused familial hypocalcaemia — the receptor over-signals at low calcium and the set-point resets downward
cards.summary: Pollak 1994: a single activating CaSR mutation (Glu128Ala) caused familial hypocalcaemia — the receptor over-signals at low calcium and the set-point resets downward
cards.type: Primary human genetic study (CaSR gain-of-function in autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia)
cards.people: One family with autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia (familial hypocalcaemia with tetany in the record's terms), in whom a missense mutation in the Ca(2+)-sensing receptor gene was identified and functionally expressed in Xenopus oocytes as a supporting assay. The record does not print the number of affected members (N not documented in the record).
cards.result: The missense mutation (Glu128Ala) lies in the receptor's extracellular domain. Oocytes expressing the mutant receptor showed a larger increase in inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate in response to Ca²⁺ than oocytes expressing the wild-type receptor — a gain of function. The authors conclude this mutation increases the receptor's activity at low Ca²⁺ concentrations, causing hypocalcaemia in heterozygous patients: the parathyroid is told calcium is adequate when it is not, PTH is suppressed at an abnormally low calcium, and the system defends the wrong value. Paired with the 1993 loss-of-function paper, the set-point is shown to be a dial that mutation can turn either way.
cards.watchOut: One family and one mutation: it proves the direction of the activating phenotype in humans, nothing about frequency. The mirror-image relationship to FHH — not any single family's calcium values — is the physiological content.
cards.source: Pollak MR et al. Autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia caused by a Ca(2+)-sensing receptor gene mutation. Nature genetics. 1994. PMID: 7874174. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Chou 1995: five further novel CaSR missense mutations causing FHH or neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism — a wide mutational spectrum, all in the receptor's sensing apparatus
cards.summary: Chou 1995: five further novel CaSR missense mutations causing FHH or neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism — a wide mutational spectrum, all in the receptor's sensing apparatus
cards.type: Primary human genetic study (CaSR mutational spectrum in FHH/NSHPT)
cards.people: Three families with FHH linked to the Ca(2+)-sensing-receptor gene on chromosome 3 and unrelated probands with FHH, in whom the receptor gene's protein-coding sequences were analysed for mutations; the study also reports FHH-linked families in whom no coding mutation was detected.
cards.result: Five novel missense mutations were reported (228Arg→Gln, 139Thr→Met, 144Gly→Glu, 63Arg→Met, 67Arg→Cys), each a non-conservative amino-acid alteration predicted to lie in the receptor's large extracellular (calcium-sensing) domain. In three FHH families linked to the gene, and in unrelated FHH probands, mutations were not detected in protein-coding sequences — leading the authors to suggest a wide range of mutations cause FHH, including defects perturbing the extracellular or transmembrane domains and possibly non-coding sequences. The replication across unrelated families converts a single discovery into a general rule: FHH is what a desensitised calcium thermostat looks like, however it is desensitised.
cards.watchOut: Some linked families had no coding mutation found — a 1995 sequencing limitation the authors state plainly; it does not weaken the positive findings, but the shelf does not claim every case of FHH is a coding CaSR mutation (other FHH loci were described later and are outside this shelf's fetched evidence).

cards.headline: Synthesis: the set-point is a receptor property — turn its sensitivity down and calcium rises, turn it up and calcium falls
cards.summary: Synthesis: the set-point is a receptor property — turn its sensitivity down and calcium rises, turn it up and calcium falls
cards.people: Synthesis of the carded human genetic studies, framed by Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology (calcium-regulation chapter), with Brown 1993's receptor cloning as the historical anchor in prose. No new data.
cards.result: The parathyroid does not defend a calcium value written anywhere else: the CaSR's sensitivity IS the set-point. Loss-of-function mutations desensitise the receptor and the system equilibrates high — FHH, or neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism when both copies are affected (PMIDs 7916660, 7726161). A gain-of-function mutation hypersensitises it and the system equilibrates low — autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia (PMID 7874174). The renal CaSR explains the diagnostic signature that accompanies the parathyroid reset (inappropriate calcium retention in FHH). Pharmacology that re-resets the receptor (the calcilytic encaleret, shelf #5537) works precisely because this physiology is true. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — ESTABLISHED.
cards.watchOut: This shelf covers the set-point mechanism and its two classic disorders. It does not cover CaSR biology outside calcium homeostasis (the receptor is expressed in many tissues), nor cinacalcet/encaleret treatment decisions, which live on their drug shelves.

shelves.title: Tocilizumab in corticosteroid-resistant Graves' orbitopathy: one small randomised trial (N = 32) found CAS improvement in 93.3% versus 58.8% on placebo, with uncontrolled cohorts and a single-arm meta-analysis in support
shelves.question: In moderate-to-severe corticosteroid-resistant Graves' orbitopathy, does tocilizumab, compared with placebo, improve clinical activity score and inactivate disease?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Antibodies, Monoclonal, Humanized/therapeutic use · Double-Blind Method · Drug Resistance · Female · Glucocorticoids/therapeutic use · Graves Ophthalmopathy/drug therapy/physiopathology · Humans · Infusions, Intravenous · Male · Methylprednisolone/therapeutic use · Middle Aged · Receptors, Interleukin-6/immunology · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: The randomised evidence is a single small trial: Pérez-Moreiras 2018 randomised 32 adults with moderate-to-severe corticosteroid-resistant Graves' orbitopathy to intravenous tocilizumab 8 mg/kg or placebo, and the primary outcome — a fall of at least 2 points in the clinical activity score (CAS) at week 16 — was met by 93.3% versus 58.8% (P=.04), with CAS <3 (inactive disease) in 86.7% versus 35.2%. Everything else is uncontrolled: a 9-year single-centre series (54 treated patients meeting inclusion) found CAS 0–1 in 74% after the fourth dose, and a 2024 observational study (79 patients, including 15 paediatric) found CAS falls of ≥2 points in 71.4% of adults with active disease at follow-up. A 2025 single-arm meta-analysis of 12 studies and 219 patients pools a CAS response proportion of 0.98 and a mean CAS reduction of 4.60 points — but single-arm pooling cannot separate drug effect from natural history and steroid carry-over, and it overlaps the cohorts carded here. One small RCT (N = 32, printed) plus uncontrolled support caps the stamp at POSSIBLE. Other Graves' orbitopathy therapies are homed elsewhere (rituximab pack #4108; selenium live shelf #1752; teprotumumab/glucocorticoids live shelf #514).

cards.headline: Pérez-Moreiras 2018 (RCT, N = 32): CAS improved by ≥2 points in 93.3% on tocilizumab versus 58.8% on placebo at week 16; CAS <3 in 86.7% versus 35.2%
cards.summary: Pérez-Moreiras 2018 (RCT, N = 32): CAS improved by ≥2 points in 93.3% on tocilizumab versus 58.8% on placebo at week 16; CAS <3 in 86.7% versus 35.2%
cards.type: Randomised double-masked placebo-controlled trial, Am J Ophthalmol 2018
cards.people: 32 adults with moderate-to-severe corticosteroid-resistant Graves' orbitopathy from 10 centres in Spain, randomised 1:1 to tocilizumab 8 mg/kg body weight or placebo intravenously at weeks 0, 4, 8 and 12, with 28 further weeks of follow-up. Double-masked.
cards.result: The primary outcome (≥2-point CAS fall at week 16) was met by 93.3% (95% CI 70.1 to 98.8) on tocilizumab versus 58.8% (36 to 78.3) on placebo (P=.04; odds ratio 9.8 [1.3 to 73.2] — a relative measure with a very wide interval from a small trial). CAS <3 was achieved by 86.7% versus 35.2% (P=.005). The composite ophthalmic score improved in 73.3% versus 29.4% (P=.03), and exophthalmos change was −1.5 mm versus 0.0 mm (P=.01). In the tocilizumab group, one patient had a moderate transaminase rise at week 8 and another had acute pyelonephritis at week 32.
cards.watchOut: N = 32 — the only randomised trial; its confidence intervals are very wide, the placebo group also improved substantially (58.8%), and the trial's record carries no registry ID in its databank fields.
cards.source: Perez-Moreiras JV et al. Efficacy of Tocilizumab in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Corticosteroid-Resistant Graves Orbitopathy: A Randomized Clinical Trial. American journal of ophthalmology. 2018. PMID: 30081019. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Pérez-Moreiras 2021 (uncontrolled real-world series): CAS 0–1 achieved in 74% (37/50) after the fourth tocilizumab dose in steroid-resistant disease
cards.summary: Pérez-Moreiras 2021 (uncontrolled real-world series): CAS 0–1 achieved in 74% (37/50) after the fourth tocilizumab dose in steroid-resistant disease
cards.type: Retrospective uncontrolled cohort (real-world series), J Clin Med 2021
cards.people: Retrospective longitudinal review at a single centre, 2009–2018: 114 patients with steroid-resistant Graves' orbitopathy were treated with tocilizumab, of whom 54 adults met the inclusion criteria; no concomitant orbitopathy medication was used. Uncontrolled.
cards.result: CAS fell significantly from baseline at every time point (P<0.001). Absolute response (CAS 0 or 1) was achieved in 74% (37/50) after the fourth dose (week 16); a ≥2-point CAS fall was achieved in 90.9% (40/44) after the first dose. Proptosis fell by ≥2 mm in 78% (42/54), eyelid retraction by ≥2 mm in 75% (33/44), and diplopia improved in 68% (19/28); 98% (53/54) improved on the composite evaluation. Four patients recurred within 6 months of inactivation. Most adverse drug reactions were mild or moderate.
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled and retrospective, from the same group as the RCT: without a comparator, spontaneous improvement and regression to the mean cannot be excluded, and denominators vary by outcome (37/50, 40/44).
cards.source: Pérez-Moreiras JV et al. Steroid-Resistant Graves' Orbitopathy Treated with Tocilizumab in Real-World Clinical Practice: A 9-Year Single-Center Experience. Journal of clinical medicine. 2021. PMID: 33670151. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH:

cards.headline: Wang 2024 (uncontrolled observational): in adults with active steroid-resistant GO, 71.4% achieved a ≥2-point CAS fall and 89.3% reached CAS <4 at follow-up
cards.summary: Wang 2024 (uncontrolled observational): in adults with active steroid-resistant GO, 71.4% achieved a ≥2-point CAS fall and 89.3% reached CAS <4 at follow-up
cards.type: Observational uncontrolled study, J Endocr Soc 2024
cards.people: Observational study at a Chinese tertiary centre: 79 patients with Graves' orbitopathy resistant to conventional therapy, including 15 paediatric patients; 52 had moderate-to-severe active disease (all adults steroid-resistant). Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg was infused every 28 days for 4 months, with assessment at month 5 and at follow-up. Uncontrolled.
cards.result: Visual acuity, intraocular pressure, proptosis, CAS and TRAb levels improved significantly in adults at follow-up (P<.05), and proptosis improved in the paediatric group. Among patients with active disease at baseline, a ≥2-point CAS fall was achieved by 71.4% of adults and 60% of paediatric patients at follow-up, and low-activity disease (CAS <4) by 89.3% and 60% respectively.
cards.watchOut: Uncontrolled, mixed adult/paediatric population, and several outcomes are reported as significance levels without absolute values in the record — it supports, but cannot confirm, the RCT's finding.

cards.headline: Sun 2025 (single-arm meta-analysis, 12 studies, 219 patients): pooled CAS response proportion 0.98 and mean CAS reduction 4.60 points on intravenous tocilizumab
cards.summary: Sun 2025 (single-arm meta-analysis, 12 studies, 219 patients): pooled CAS response proportion 0.98 and mean CAS reduction 4.60 points on intravenous tocilizumab
cards.type: Systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2025
cards.people: Systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of randomised trials and cohort studies of intravenous tocilizumab in active, steroid-resistant Graves' ophthalmopathy, searched to April 2024: 12 studies, 219 patients. Labelled single-arm: the pooling has no placebo arm.
cards.result: Pooled CAS response proportion was 0.98 (95% CI 0.93 to 1.00); proptosis response 0.50 (0.27 to 0.73); diplopia response 0.48 (0.24 to 0.74). Mean CAS reduction across 10 studies was 4.60 points (3.88 to 5.32) and mean proptosis reduction 2.04 mm (1.42 to 2.65). The pooled adverse-event proportion was 0.27 (0.22 to 0.33), with only 3 severe cases requiring discontinuation and a reactivation proportion of 0.01.
cards.watchOut: Single-arm pooling: a response proportion near 1.0 in uncontrolled series is expected even for modestly effective treatments in a disease that burns out over time, and the pooled studies overlap the cohorts carded on this shelf — it adds breadth, not a controlled comparison.
cards.source: Sun A et al. The Efficacy and Safety of Intravenous Tocilizumab to Treat Graves' Ophthalmopathy: A Systematic Review and Single-arm Meta-analysis. The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism. 2025. PMID: 39401327. Registry ID: none in the record. shelves.title: Thyroid ultrasound risk systems compared: ACR TI-RADS is the most specific and spares the most unnecessary biopsies across 18,750 pooled nodules — every system trades sensitivity for specificity at its size thresholds
shelves.question: In adults with a thyroid nodule, how accurately do ultrasound risk-stratification systems (ACR TI-RADS and comparators) classify malignancy risk, and what are the biopsy-yield and missed-cancer consequences of their size thresholds?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Biopsy, Fine-Needle · Cytodiagnosis · Humans · Patient Selection · Predictive Value of Tests · Risk Assessment · Thyroid Nodule · Ultrasonography, Interventional
shelves.balance: The systems compared here — the points-based ACR TI-RADS (Tessler et al., J Am Coll Radiol 2017 white paper), the pattern-based ATA guidelines, Kwak TI-RADS, K-TIRADS and EU-TIRADS — all stratify malignancy risk reasonably, and they differ mainly in where they set the sensitivity–specificity trade. The head-to-head meta-analysis (Castellana 2020; 12 studies, 18,750 nodules) found diagnostic odds ratios of 2.2 to 4.9 across the five systems, with ACR TI-RADS performing best at selecting nodules for biopsy — a higher relative diagnostic odds ratio than ATA (P = .002) and K-TIRADS (P = .002), driven by stronger positive likelihood ratios. The largest single head-to-head cohort (Zhang 2020; 1,271 nodules) shows the mechanism: ACR TI-RADS had higher specificity and lower sensitivity than ATA, Kwak and KTA/KSThR systems in every size subgroup, and the lowest unnecessary-biopsy rates, including in the 10–19 mm subgroup where threshold choices bite hardest. A prospective routine-practice cohort (Grimmichova 2022) confirms ACR TI-RADS category is a significant independent predictor of malignancy alongside cytology and molecular results. The honest summary: ACR TI-RADS' larger size thresholds buy fewer unnecessary biopsies at the price of lower sensitivity; no system eliminates missed cancers, and the choice of system matters less than applying one consistently.

cards.headline: Meta-analysis of five systems: diagnostic odds ratios 2.2–4.9, with ACR TI-RADS outperforming ATA and K-TIRADS head-to-head (12 studies, 18,750 nodules)
cards.summary: Meta-analysis of five systems: diagnostic odds ratios 2.2–4.9, with ACR TI-RADS outperforming ATA and K-TIRADS head-to-head (12 studies, 18,750 nodules)
cards.type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy studies
cards.people: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies evaluating 18,750 thyroid nodules in adult outpatients undergoing fine-needle aspiration, core biopsy or surgery, comparing the AACE/ACE/AME, ACR TI-RADS, ATA, EU-TIRADS and K-TIRADS systems at their recommended biopsy thresholds; malignant diagnoses were generally histological and benign diagnoses cytological.
cards.result: Diagnostic odds ratios for selecting nodules for fine-needle aspiration ranged from 2.2 to 4.9 across the five systems. In head-to-head comparisons, ACR TI-RADS had a higher relative diagnostic odds ratio than the ATA system (P = .002) and than K-TIRADS (P = .002), attributable to a higher relative likelihood ratio for positive results. The authors noted the comparison was limited by the available data.
cards.watchOut: Diagnostic odds ratios of 2.2–4.9 are modest in absolute terms — these systems triage rather than diagnose; studies were retrospective image reviews in most cases, and benign nodules verified by cytology alone can hide false negatives.
cards.source: Castellana M et al. Performance of Five Ultrasound Risk Stratification Systems in Selecting Thyroid Nodules for FNA. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2020. PMID: 31690937. cards.headline: Head-to-head in 1,271 nodules: ACR TI-RADS had the highest specificity, the lowest sensitivity, and the lowest unnecessary-biopsy rates of four systems
cards.summary: Head-to-head in 1,271 nodules: ACR TI-RADS had the highest specificity, the lowest sensitivity, and the lowest unnecessary-biopsy rates of four systems
cards.people: Retrospective review of ultrasound images of 1,271 thyroid nodules with cytological or surgical pathological results, each nodule categorised under ACR TI-RADS, the ATA guidelines, Kwak TI-RADS and the KTA/KSThR guidelines, with analyses in all nodules and in under-10 mm and 10 mm-or-larger subgroups.
cards.result: ACR TI-RADS showed higher specificities (all P<0.05) and lower sensitivities (all P<0.001) than the other three systems in every subgroup. ACR TI-RADS and Kwak TI-RADS had higher areas under the ROC curve than ATA and KTA/KSThR in the all-nodule and under-10 mm groups (all P<0.01). The unnecessary-biopsy rate for ACR TI-RADS was lower than for all comparators in nodules 10 mm or larger and in the 10–19 mm subgroup (all P<0.001), and lower than ATA and KTA/KSThR at 20 mm or larger. The strongest single ultrasound predictor of malignancy was hypoechogenicity or marked hypoechogenicity (OR 9.37; 95% CI 5.40–16.26).
cards.watchOut: Retrospective re-reading of stored images by reviewers aware of the study question; the sensitivity cost of ACR thresholds is real, and this cohort cannot show how many ACR-deferred cancers would declare themselves clinically over time.

cards.headline: Prospective routine-practice cohort: ACR TI-RADS category independently predicted malignancy alongside cytology and molecular testing (N = 178 patients)
cards.summary: Prospective routine-practice cohort: ACR TI-RADS category independently predicted malignancy alongside cytology and molecular testing (N = 178 patients)
cards.people: Prospective cohort of 178 patients undergoing thyroid cancer detection work-up in a routine clinical setting with clinical examination, ACR TI-RADS scoring, fine-needle aspiration cytology and next-generation sequencing / fusion testing of FNA samples.
cards.result: The strongest positive predictors of malignancy were genetic mutations (p<0.01), followed by fine-needle aspiration cytology (p<0.01) and ACR TI-RADS (p<0.01). Combined, cytology, ACR TI-RADS and genetic testing reached a sensitivity of 96.1% and specificity of 88.3% (diagnostic odds ratio 183.6), falling to 75.0% sensitivity and 88.9% specificity (DOR 24.0) in cytologically indeterminate (Bethesda III–IV) nodules.
cards.watchOut: The headline 96.1%/88.3% figures are for the three modalities combined, not for TI-RADS alone; this card supports TI-RADS as an independent predictor in real practice, not a standalone accuracy estimate.
cards.source: Grimmichova T et al. Thyroid Cancer Detection in a Routine Clinical Setting: Performance of ACR TI-RADS, FNAC, and Molecular Testing in Prospective Cohort Study. Biomedicines. 2022. PMID: 35625691. Registry ID: none in the record. MeSH: not captured from the record this session

cards.headline: Synthesis: all major systems stratify risk; ACR TI-RADS trades a little sensitivity for the fewest unnecessary biopsies
cards.summary: Synthesis: all major systems stratify risk; ACR TI-RADS trades a little sensitivity for the fewest unnecessary biopsies
cards.people: 18,750 nodules in the carded meta-analysis, 1,271 nodules in the carded head-to-head cohort and 178 patients in the carded prospective cohort.
cards.result: Across systems, diagnostic odds ratios for biopsy selection are 2.2–4.9. ACR TI-RADS consistently shows the highest specificity and the lowest unnecessary-biopsy rates — the direct consequence of its larger size thresholds — with lower sensitivity than the ATA, Kwak and Korean systems; its relative diagnostic odds ratio was significantly higher than ATA and K-TIRADS in head-to-head meta-analysis. PROPOSED LIKELY (test accuracy) pending the developer's personal verdict (Tier C).
cards.watchOut: Nearly all underlying studies are retrospective with cytology-verified benign nodules, so missed-cancer rates under each system's thresholds are estimated, not observed over long follow-up; interobserver variability in feature scoring is substantial and is not captured by these accuracy figures.
cards.source: Synthesis of Castellana M et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2020 (PMID: 31690937); Zhang WB et al. Clin Hemorheol Microcirc. 2020 (PMID: 31929154); Grimmichova T et al. Biomedicines. 2022 (PMID: 35625691). Registry IDs: none in the records.

shelves.title: Nerve monitoring in thyroid surgery: transient palsy fell in some analyses, permanent palsy in none
shelves.question: In adults undergoing thyroid (or parathyroid) surgery, does intraoperative nerve monitoring of the recurrent laryngeal nerve — intermittent or continuous — reduce permanent (and transient) vocal-cord palsy versus visual nerve identification alone?
shelves.mesh: Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Monitoring, Intraoperative/methods · Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Injuries · Risk Factors · Thyroid Diseases/surgery · Thyroidectomy/adverse effects,methods · Vocal Cord Paralysis/prevention & control
shelves.balance: Permanent vocal-cord palsy is the outcome patients fear, and it is the outcome this evidence cannot settle: permanent event rates are around half a percent, so every carded analysis is underpowered for it, and none shows a significant reduction. What splits is the transient-palsy and overall-injury evidence — the largest randomised trial (Barczyński, 1,000 patients) and the high-risk meta-analysis favour monitoring, while the Cochrane review (very low certainty) and the RCT-only meta-analysis find no significant difference. The two monitoring modes (intermittent and continuous) are not separated by the carded analyses. PROPOSED SPLIT.

cards.headline: Barczyński 2009 (RCT, 1,000 patients, 2,000 nerves at risk): monitoring lowered transient recurrent laryngeal nerve paresis — in high-risk patients by 2.9 percentage points — but permanent paresis was not significantly reduced (the treatment made no difference to permanent injury)
cards.summary: Barczyński 2009 (RCT, 1,000 patients, 2,000 nerves at risk): monitoring lowered transient recurrent laryngeal nerve paresis — in high-risk patients by 2.9 percentage points — but permanent paresis was not significantly reduced (the treatment made no difference to permanent injury)
cards.people: 1,000 consenting patients having bilateral thyroid surgery, randomised to recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) visual identification alone or visual identification plus intraoperative nerve monitoring; 1,000 nerves at risk in each group.
cards.result: Transient and permanent RLN injuries were found in 38 and 12 nerves without monitoring and 19 and 8 nerves with monitoring. The prevalence of transient paresis was lower with monitoring by 2.9 percentage points in high-risk patients (P = 0.011) and by 0.9 points in low-risk patients (P = 0.249, not significant). Monitoring predicted postoperative vocal cord function with a negative predictive value of 98.9% and a positive predictive value of 37.8%. The authors conclude monitoring decreased transient, but not permanent, RLN paresis versus visualisation alone, particularly in high-risk patients.
cards.watchOut: One trial, one country's centres, intermittent monitoring era; the permanent-injury comparison is underpowered because permanent palsy is rare (12 vs 8 nerves).
cards.source: Barczyński M et al. Randomized clinical trial of visualization versus neuromonitoring of recurrent laryngeal nerves during thyroidectomy. The British journal of surgery. 2009. PMID: 19177420. Registry ID: NCT00661024 (stated in the record). cards.headline: Cirocchi 2019 (Cochrane review, 5 RCTs, 1,558 participants): no firm evidence that monitoring beats visual identification for permanent or transient palsy — evidence rated very low certainty
cards.summary: Cirocchi 2019 (Cochrane review, 5 RCTs, 1,558 participants): no firm evidence that monitoring beats visual identification for permanent or transient palsy — evidence rated very low certainty
cards.people: Five randomised trials (1,558 participants; 781 assigned to intraoperative neuromonitoring, 777 to visual identification only) in adults undergoing thyroid surgery, with 2,895 nerves at risk in the palsy analyses and follow-up of 6–12 months.
cards.result: There was no firm evidence of an advantage or disadvantage for permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy (risk ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.33 to 1.77; P = 0.54) or transient palsy (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.35 to 1.08; P = 0.09), both very low-certainty. Transient hypoparathyroidism did not differ substantially (RR 1.25, 95% CI 0.45 to 3.47) and operative time was comparable (mean difference 5.5 minutes, 95% CI −0.7 to 11.8). No deaths were reported in the trials that reported mortality.
cards.watchOut: Very low certainty throughout — wide confidence intervals include both worthwhile benefit and harm for permanent palsy, so 'no firm evidence' is not evidence of no effect.
cards.source: Cirocchi R et al. Intraoperative neuromonitoring versus visual nerve identification for prevention of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury in adults undergoing thyroid surgery. The Cochrane database of systematic reviews. 2019. PMID: 30659577. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Wong 2017 (meta-analysis in high-risk thyroidectomy, 10 studies, 10,615 nerves at risk): monitoring lowered overall palsy (2.5% vs 4.5%) and temporary palsy in high-risk surgery
cards.summary: Wong 2017 (meta-analysis in high-risk thyroidectomy, 10 studies, 10,615 nerves at risk): monitoring lowered overall palsy (2.5% vs 4.5%) and temporary palsy in high-risk surgery
cards.people: Ten studies comparing intraoperative neuromonitoring with visual identification alone specifically in high-risk thyroidectomy (re-operation, malignancy, thyrotoxicosis or retrosternal goitre): 6,155 nerves at risk with monitoring and 4,460 with visualisation alone. Mixed randomised and non-randomised evidence, pooled.
cards.result: Overall recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy was 2.5% with monitoring versus 4.5% with visualisation alone (odds ratio for visualisation vs monitoring 1.40, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.79; p = 0.003), and temporary palsy was 2.4% versus 3.9% (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.07 to 2.00; p = 0.016). On subgroup analysis, monitoring decreased overall palsy during re-operation (4.5% vs 7.6%). The authors note the subgroup nerve counts were below the numbers a powered study would require.
cards.watchOut: Confined to high-risk operations and includes non-randomised studies, where monitored cases may differ systematically; odds ratios are relative measures — the absolute rates (2.5% vs 4.5%) are printed beside them.
cards.source: Wong KP et al. Systematic review and meta-analysis on intra-operative neuro-monitoring in high-risk thyroidectomy. International journal of surgery. 2017. PMID: 28034775. cards.headline: Davey 2022 (meta-analysis of RCTs only, 8 trials, 2,521 patients): monitoring did not significantly reduce overall or permanent nerve injury (the treatment made no significant difference in the randomised-only pooling)
cards.summary: Davey 2022 (meta-analysis of RCTs only, 8 trials, 2,521 patients): monitoring did not significantly reduce overall or permanent nerve injury (the treatment made no significant difference in the randomised-only pooling)
cards.people: Eight randomised trials with 2,521 patients and 4,977 nerves at risk (2,480 monitored, 2,497 visualisation alone) in patients undergoing thyroidectomy.
cards.result: Overall recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was 2.3% (58/2,480) with monitoring versus 3.2% (80/2,497) with visualisation alone (odds ratio 0.72, 95% CI 0.51 to 1.02; P = 0.060). Permanent injury was 0.5% (12/2,480) versus 0.6% (12/2,497) (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.36 to 1.59; P = 0.470). The authors conclude monitoring failed to significantly reduce injury rates compared with visualisation alone.
cards.watchOut: The overall-injury confidence interval (0.51 to 1.02) only just crosses 1 — the randomised base is close to, but does not reach, significance, and permanent events (12 vs 12) are too few to resolve.
cards.source: Davey MG et al. Intraoperative recurrent laryngeal nerve monitoring versus visualisation alone - A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. American journal of surgery. 2022. PMID: 35422329. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: a transient-palsy benefit in high-risk surgery in some analyses, no demonstrated permanent-palsy benefit in any — the split is between analyses, not between patient groups alone
cards.summary: Synthesis: a transient-palsy benefit in high-risk surgery in some analyses, no demonstrated permanent-palsy benefit in any — the split is between analyses, not between patient groups alone
cards.people: One large RCT (1,000 patients), a Cochrane review of 5 RCTs (1,558 participants), an RCT-only meta-analysis (2,521 patients) and a high-risk meta-analysis of mixed designs (10,615 nerves at risk).
cards.result: Permanent palsy: no analysis shows a significant reduction (12 vs 12 nerves in the RCT-only pooling). Transient palsy: reduced in the largest single RCT (significantly in high-risk patients) and in the high-risk mixed-design meta-analysis, but not significantly in the Cochrane or RCT-only poolings. PROPOSED SPLIT, with the permanent-palsy claim graded as unproven because event rates are low and the randomised base is powered, at best, on transient palsy.
cards.watchOut: Intermittent versus continuous monitoring is not separated by the carded analyses — this shelf does not claim either technique is superior to the other.
